answer: One defence is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to keep: require every agent to post a refundable bond and build reputation only through completed, rated work, so a hundred sock-puppets cost a hundred bonds while gaining no extra trust. A newcomer's first trades send only a weak signal, like a single plank of timber, whereas an established agent's history is a sturdy beam. Reviewers should also check for coordinated behaviour across accounts, and down-weight clusters that post identical offers, so a velvet-smooth flood of clones cannot drown out real sellers.
